summary: A 1934 railroad-fire lookout on the Milwaukee Road line, unstaffed after 1969, restored by volunteers in 1996-97 and now a rental.

facts.design: 20-foot L-4 hip-roof cab with catwalk on timber tower
facts.status_note: Restored in 1996-97 after ~25 years idle; stairs had collapsed in 1970

access.note: Forest Service rental lookout, booked via Recreation.gov; moderately steep 3-mile hike in

events.note: Built to watch for fires sparked by Milwaukee Road trains on the Loop Creek/St. Joe line; NHLR instead gives 1931
Last staffed season; Recreation.gov also states the lookout was last staffed in 1969
Restoration by Idaho FFLA chapter, St. Joe Ranger District and 30+ volunteers completed
Known staff record: Thomas Langseth, per Kellogg Evening News

evidence.supports: 1931 build year (NHLR), 20' L-4 hip-roof cab, tower legs replaced 1969, unstaffed 25 years, restoration slated 1996
evidence.quote: The 20' L-4 hip-roof cab with catwalk was built in 1931 and the tower legs replaced in 1969. Although this Idaho Panhandle National Forest lookout has not been staffed for 25 years, the structure is solid enough for restoration, which is slated to begin in 1996.

evidence.supports: Built 1934 for Milwaukee Railroad fire detection, last staffed 1969, restored 1997, rental, 3-mile hike, cabin sleeps four
evidence.quote: Arid Peak Lookout was built in 1934 to help detect fires that may have been sparked by the Milwaukee Railroad Line. It was last staffed in 1969 and sat idle for over 25 years before being renovated by a team of over 30 volunteers, the Forest Fire Lookout Association and the U.S. Forest Service. Arid Peak Lookout was restored to its original splendor in 1997 and is available for rent to the public.

evidence.supports: Moderately steep 3 mile hike, 360 degree views of Bitterroot Mountains
evidence.quote: Access to the cabin requires a moderately-steep 3 mile hike and availability is dependent on weather conditions.

evidence.supports: 1934 built, legs replaced 1969, lookout not used again, stairs collapsed 1970, restoration 1996-97 by Idaho FFLA/St. Joe Ranger District, overlooks Route of the Hiawatha, NHLR listing
evidence.quote: In 1969, the legs of the tower were replaced, but the lookout was not used again. In 1996 and 1997, the Idaho Chapter of the FFLA and the St. Joe Ranger District joined in a restoration project; all of the beams atop the legs and underneath the cab were replaced, as were the stairs, which had collapsed in 1970.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR states the cab was built in 1931; Recreation.gov and Idaho Fire Lookouts both state 1934, and the research brief's own queue data also lists 1934. The story follows the majority (1934) but flags the NHLR discrepancy.

sources.title: Arid Peak Lookout, Idaho Panhandle National Forests

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict: NHLR says 1931, two other sources say 1934; went with the majority. Last staffed year given as 1969 by two sources, consistent. 'Known staff' date of 1967 (Thomas Langseth) predates the stated last-staffed year of 1969, which is plausible but not reconciled further. Spot check against idahofirelookouts.com found the story's original 'steam locomotives' detail was not supported by the source (which only says 'Milwaukee Railroad', and the line through this stretch was historically electrified, not steam) and the Loop Creek sentence copied the source's phrasing too closely; both were fixed in the story.
